title: Sharp Joint Regions for Benefits of Several Monotone Binary Causes under Common Confounding
banked_reason: The proposal omits LiPearl2024 and ShuWangLi2026, close multivalued-PoC treatments whose multi-hypothetical targets must be mapped against the Boolean-lattice region; tier=letter below novelty_target=field, so the kernel needs a broader named query class or demonstrated consequence to meet the floor.
gap_reasons: The proposal omits LiPearl2024 and ShuWangLi2026, close multivalued-PoC treatments whose multi-hypothetical targets must be mapped against the Boolean-lattice region; tier=letter below novelty_target=field, so the kernel needs a broader named query class or demonstrated consequence to meet the floor.
proof_attempt_summary: Three proposal-review rounds tested the all-m factual-support, gluing, singleton-facet, and compressed-compiler package against generic selection, transport, response-signature, and multivalued probability-of-causation prior art. The mathematical package remained a plausible letter/subfield result, but no faithful field-tier strengthening was supported: reaching the floor would require a proved structural classification for a broader named class of higher-order co-benefit queries. The all-m proofs and the precise comparisons to LiPearl2024 and ShuWangLi2026 remain unfinished obligations.
tldr: Given a strictly positive observational law for several binary causes and a binary outcome, what is the complete sharp joint region of the coordinatewise-monotone baseline-to-singleton benefit indicators under arbitrary common confounding? The two headline results are the all-\(m\) four-case factual-support lemma and the sharp singleton theorem with \(m+m2^{m-1}\) irredundant causal attribution facets, a linear-size lift, and an exact scalar/pairwise sufficiency boundary at \(m=2\). The full-law transport region, sharp scalar co-benefit bound, gluing construction, and support-aggregated compiler are consequences. The defensible novelty is only the closed causal support evaluation and resulting identification formula; the project is explicitly assessed below a field-level contribution because all generic LP, selection, transport, quotient, and SCM-attainment machinery is prior art.
gap: Hashimoto–Kawakami–Tian already give a sharp generic joint-potential-outcome LP that covers the Boolean-lattice model after categorical expansion; Rossetto–Antonucci give generic response-signature quotient and attainment machinery; Artstein and Gale give the selection/transport characterization. Kawakami–Kuroki–Tian identify a different pairwise threshold-crossing vector PoC under conditional exogeneity, conditional no-crossing or structural-function monotonicity, and common-support conditions, and Sani–Mastakouri–Janzing bound one binary-treatment PNS by combining two causal marginals in a Markovian collider model. The remaining defensible gap is narrower: no inspected source evaluates arbitrary-confounding coordinatewise Boolean-lattice monotonicity into the four factual supports and the \(2m\)-summary complete singleton facet family for the joint vector \((B_i)\).
fill: Make \(\mathrm{lem{:}factual\text{-}support}\) and \(\mathrm{thm{:}singleton\text{-}facets}\) the contribution: prove the support table and its legal monotone completions, then derive the singleton Minkowski representation, full irredundant facet family, linear lift, separation oracle, and exact scalar/pairwise boundary. Retain the full-law capacity, scalar co-benefit interval, independent gluing, and compiler only as operational consequences with Artstein/Gale/Hashimoto–Kawakami–Tian/Rossetto–Antonucci priority explicit.
